activities.title: High-contrast mobile
activities.description: A simple black-and-white or high-contrast mobile hung within focal range above where the baby lies, to support early visual development.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Hang at roughly 20-30cm from the baby's face, not directly over a crib mattress if unsupervised.

activities.title: Topponcino handling
activities.description: Using a small, firm pillow (topponcino) to move and hold a newborn gently and consistently, supporting the baby's sense of security.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Keep it consistently in the same spot near the changing/resting area.

activities.title: Ring on a ribbon (reach and grasp)
activities.description: A wooden ring hung at chest height, within reach, to invite intentional reaching, batting, and grasping.
activities.materialsNeeded: Wooden ring, ribbon, low stand or frame
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Position on a low mat, not a crib, so movement is unrestricted.

activities.title: Floor mat with mirror
activities.description: A firm, flat mat with an unbreakable mirror at floor level, encouraging tummy time, head lifting, and self-observation.
activities.materialsNeeded: Firm play mat, acrylic (unbreakable) wall mirror mounted low
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Mirror mounted securely at the child's eye level while lying or sitting.

activities.title: Object permanence box with tray
activities.description: A box with a hole where a ball is dropped in and disappears into a tray below, reinforced by retrieving it — supports the emerging understanding that objects continue to exist unseen.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Present on a low shelf at the child's own height, not handed over each time.

activities.title: Treasure basket
activities.description: A low, sturdy basket of everyday natural-material objects (wooden spoon, pinecone, shell, fabric swatch) for open-ended sensory exploration while seated.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Rotate objects periodically; supervise closely for choking hazards.

activities.title: Push/pull walker toy
activities.description: A sturdy, weighted push toy that supports early cruising and independent walking practice.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Clear a straight, open path along low furniture the child can cruise along.

activities.title: Simple shape sorter
activities.description: A wooden box or cube with one or two shape cut-outs, refining hand-eye coordination and an early sense of order.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Start with a single shape; add more shapes only once one is mastered.

activities.title: Pouring water, jug to jug
activities.description: Pouring a small amount of water between two small pitchers, building concentration, coordination, and independence.
activities.materialsNeeded: Two small stainless-steel or glass pitchers, tray, sponge
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Set up on a low tray at a table the child can reach; a small towel nearby for spills.

activities.title: 3-piece ring stacker
activities.description: Stacking a small number of graduated rings onto a post, refining grasp and an early sense of size sequencing.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Keep on the active low shelf at consistent placement.

activities.title: Naming real objects
activities.description: Naming everyday real objects (cup, spoon, shoe) clearly and consistently during daily routines, rather than relying on picture books alone at this age.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Use the real word, not a diminutive substitute, so vocabulary is accurate from the start.

activities.title: Spooning dry beans between bowls
activities.description: Transferring dried beans or chickpeas from one small bowl to another with a spoon, refining wrist control and concentration.
activities.materialsNeeded: Two small bowls, spoon, dried beans, tray
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Use a tray to contain spills; start with larger beans before smaller ones.

activities.title: Wiping up a spill
activities.description: A small sponge and bowl kept accessible so the child can independently wipe up their own spills as part of daily practical life.
activities.materialsNeeded: Small sponge, small bowl or basin
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Keep the sponge station at the child's height near the eating/water area.

activities.title: Sorting by color
activities.description: Sorting a small set of objects into groups by a single quality (color), an early exercise in visual discrimination and classification.
activities.materialsNeeded: Small bowls, objects/pom-poms in 2-3 distinct colors
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Start with just two colors, add a third only once that's easy.

activities.title: Dressing frame: large buttons
activities.description: A frame with two fabric panels joined by large buttons, isolating and practicing the fastening motion used in dressing.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Introduce one dressing frame type at a time (buttons, then zippers, then snaps).

activities.title: Knobbed cylinder blocks
activities.description: Classic Montessori material: cylinders of varying diameter and/or height, removed and replaced into matching sockets, refining visual discrimination of dimension.
activities.materialsNeeded: Knobbed cylinder block (one of the four variations)
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Introduce one block at a time; work on a mat so pieces don't roll away.

activities.title: Pink tower
activities.description: Ten pink wooden cubes of graduated size, stacked largest to smallest, refining visual-spatial discrimination of size in three dimensions.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Needs floor space to build; carry cubes with two hands, one at a time.

activities.title: Sandpaper letters
activities.description: Letters cut from sandpaper mounted on boards, traced with two fingers while saying the letter's sound, connecting the visual, tactile, and phonetic.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Introduce sounds, not letter names, in small groups of three.

activities.title: Care of a plant
activities.description: Watering, wiping leaves, and observing a real houseplant kept at the child's height, building responsibility and care for the environment.
activities.materialsNeeded: Small watering can, a hardy houseplant at low height
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Choose a resilient plant so early over/under-watering isn't discouraging.

activities.title: Brown stair
activities.description: Ten wooden prisms graduated in thickness, arranged from thickest to thinnest, refining discrimination of a single dimension (width).
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Best on a floor mat; often paired with the pink tower once both are known.

activities.title: Moveable alphabet, simple words
activities.description: Building simple phonetic words with cut-out letters before handwriting is fluent, letting composition outpace the physical skill of writing.
activities.materialsNeeded: Moveable alphabet box, small objects/picture cards for simple 3-letter words
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Best introduced only after most sandpaper letter sounds are known.

activities.title: Number rods
activities.description: Ten rods of increasing length in alternating red/blue decimeter segments, connecting a physical quantity to a number name.
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Needs a long, clear floor mat to lay all ten rods out.

activities.title: Table washing
activities.description: A full, ordered practical-life sequence — wetting, soaping, scrubbing, rinsing, drying a small table — combining many refined movements in one purposeful task.
activities.materialsNeeded: Small basin, apron, brush, soap, sponge, drying cloth, small table
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Model the full sequence once, slowly, before inviting the child to try it independently.

activities.title: Metal insets, tracing and coloring
activities.description: Tracing geometric metal insets and filling them with colored pencil lines, building the pencil control needed for handwriting.
activities.materialsNeeded: Metal insets set, colored pencils, plain paper
activities.preparedEnvironmentTips: Encourage consistent line direction over speed or coverage.

sensitivePeriods.description: An intense drive to refine gross motor control — reaching, crawling, walking, climbing, and later fine coordination.
Rapid, largely effortless absorption of spoken (and later written) language; peaks in the first three years.
A strong preference for consistency and predictability in routines, sequences, and the placement of objects in the environment.
Fascination with tiny details and small items, refining the pincer grasp and close visual attention.
Heightened interest in comparing and classifying sensory qualities — size, color, texture, sound, weight.
Interest in precise, purposeful, sequenced physical actions rather than movement for its own sake.
Growing ability to combine multiple refined movements into a single purposeful task.
A drive toward doing things for oneself — dressing, eating, cleaning up — often expressed as 'help me do it myself.'
Interest in the social forms of a community — greetings, turn-taking, polite requests — through observation and repetition.
